turns.speaker: Melanie
turns.text: Hey, you got a sec? I need to flag something weird in the query log.

turns.speaker: Colleague
turns.text: Sure, what's up? I was just about to grab coffee, but this sounds urgent.

turns.speaker: Melanie
turns.text: So, I was debugging the search endpoint and I accidentally logged the full request body — including the customer's email and phone number. It's sitting in the query log right now.

turns.speaker: Colleague
turns.text: Oh no. That's sensitive data. Did you scrub it or rotate the log?

turns.speaker: Melanie
turns.text: I already deleted the entries and added a filter to strip PII before logging. But I wanted you to know in case anyone else saw it.

turns.speaker: Colleague
turns.text: Good catch. At least it's contained. But let's add a ticket to audit the logging pipeline — we can't have that happen again.

turns.speaker: Melanie
turns.text: Agreed. Also, on a lighter note — I finally added pagination to the API. The response size was getting out of hand.

turns.speaker: Colleague
turns.text: Nice, that's been on the backlog for weeks. Did you test it with the big dataset?

turns.speaker: Melanie
turns.text: Yeah, I ran a quick load test locally. It held up fine under heavy load — no timeouts, memory stayed flat.

turns.speaker: Colleague
turns.text: Morning. Quick question — did you deploy the pagination change yesterday? I saw a new version in staging.

turns.speaker: Melanie
turns.text: Yeah, I pushed it to prod last night. I know I should have run the test suite first, but I was in a hurry to get it out before the demo.

turns.speaker: Colleague
turns.text: Uh, Melanie... you deployed without running the test suite? That's risky.

turns.speaker: Melanie
turns.text: I know, I know. I figured it was a small change, what could go wrong?

turns.speaker: Colleague
turns.text: Well, I just got a ping from support — the export endpoint is returning duplicate rows. Looks like a regression slipped into production.

turns.speaker: Melanie
turns.text: Damn. That's probably because I changed the pagination offset logic but didn't update the export query. I'll roll back and fix it now.

turns.speaker: Colleague
turns.text: Let's do a proper hotfix this time — and please, run the tests before you redeploy. I'll help you write a regression test for this exact case.

turns.speaker: Melanie
turns.text: You're right. I'm sorry. I'll never skip the suite again — this is exactly why we have it.

turns.speaker: Melanie
turns.text: Hey, just wanted to update you — the hotfix is live, and I ran the full test suite this time. All green.

turns.speaker: Colleague
turns.text: Good to hear. And the duplicate rows issue?

turns.speaker: Melanie
turns.text: Fixed. The regression was in the pagination cursor — I was using the wrong key. Now the export and the list endpoint share the same logic.

turns.speaker: Colleague
turns.text: Nice. Also, I checked the query log from earlier — the PII filter is working. No more sensitive data leaking into the logs.

turns.speaker: Melanie
turns.text: Great. That was a close call. I'm just glad we caught it before it hit the customer-facing logs.

turns.speaker: Colleague
turns.text: Yeah, and the API held up under heavy load during the demo yesterday — so the pagination change is solid now. Let's just keep the test suite mandatory from now on.

turns.speaker: Melanie
turns.text: Absolutely. Lesson learned. Thanks for having my back on this.
